Many a northern Ohio resident has driven through the beautiful

Chagrin River Valley, following the winding river to Kirtland,

Ohio. As the visitor approaches

the last hill from the valley floor, he sees a majestic building known in the area as "the old Mormon temple,"which stands as a memorial to the nearly 4,000 Saints who settled in and around Kirtland in the 1830s. Now, after

135 years, little remains of the original community. The land is

rapidly being taken up by suburban residents of Cleveland;

industries in the city have long since disappeared. The accompanying photographs show what

remains today of this historic community.

the beating the rest of their lives.

This recently restored house was the home of President Sidney Rigdon. A former minister of a

In September 1831, Joseph Smith and his family moved to the Johnson farmhouse at Hiram, about 30 miles southeast of Kirtland.
